resolutions.rationale: Rauser expressly qualifies that not every Christian uses maximal-greatness terminology and presents worship-worthiness as following within that Christian conception, without claiming this opening definition independently proves the conception true.

Rauser fairly stresses genre, historical distance, and occasional scholarly help, but his claim that Barker would toss everything out if readers cannot grasp a text perfectly is a materially stronger position than Barker's actual expert-disagreement challenge.

Barker explicitly acknowledges the human speaker, yet he frames human speech in canon as forcing a choice between direct divine speech and discarding the text, understating Rauser's intermediate account of preserved lament within an inspired canon.

Barker correctly identifies that Rauser's framework is conditional on Christian commitments, but his assertion that the framework makes contrary evidence impossible overstates a position Rauser presents as assumption-dependent and open to critique and fallibility.

Barker preserves the possibility of metaphor and points to punitive divine agency, but the categorical label that God is a rapist compresses distinctions among metaphorical self-attribution, authorization of invasion, and direct physical agency.

The victim-centered thought experiment directly tests whether later redemptive framing answers immediate harm, but calling the depicted people peaceful and loving and alternative Christian accounts twisted overstates contested details before separating the surveyed readings.

No distinct pro-side debate-wide consequence remains outside the locked moves: the Christian conception, interpretive framework, conquest diversity, and broad-message claims are already represented, so any adjustment would duplicate move-level assessment.

No distinct con-side debate-wide consequence remains outside the locked moves: communication failure, divine agency, victim-centered harm, and recurring violence are already represented, so any adjustment would duplicate move-level assessment.
